'''G. Seth Shostak''' (born July 20, 1943) is an American [[astronomer]] and author, and is currently the senior astronomer for the [[SETI Institute]].<ref name="US-20140521">{{cite web |last=Shostak |first=Seth |title=Using Radio in the Search for Extraterrestrial Intelligence |url=https://science.house.gov/sites/republicans.science.house.gov/files/documents/HHRG-113-SY-WState-SShostak-20140521.pdf |date=21 May 2014 |work=[[US Congress]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180924002658/https://science.house.gov/sites/republicans.science.house.gov/files/documents/HHRG-113-SY-WState-SShostak-20140521.pdf |access-date=22 May 2014 |archive-date=2018-09-24 }}</ref><ref name="ABC-20140521">{{cite news |last=Kleineidam |first=Alina |title=Astronomers tell Congress they're almost certain ET exists |url=https://abcnews.go.com/blogs/politics/2014/05/astronomers-tell-congress-almost-certain-et-exists/ |date=21 May 2014 |work=[[ABC News (United States)|ABC News]] |access-date=22 May 2014 |archive-date=22 May 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140522105049/http://abcnews.go.com/blogs/politics/2014/05/astronomers-tell-congress-almost-certain-et-exists/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.theskepticsguide.org/ |title=Skeptics Guide to the Universe podcast 582 2016-09-03 |access-date=2016-09-05 |archive-date=2006-04-17 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060417155253/http://www.theskepticsguide.org/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

Shostak co-hosts the weekly radio show/[[podcast]] ''[[Big Picture Science]]'', has played himself numerous times in TV and internet film dramas, and has acted in several science fiction films.

==Early life and education==
Seth Shostak was born in a Jewish family in [[Arlington County, Virginia]], the son of Arthur and Bertha Shostak (née Gortenburg); his father was an electrical engineer.<ref>{{cite web |title=1950 United States Federal Census |url=https://www.ancestry.com/sharing/29423504?h=ff5052 |website=Ancestry.com |access-date=12 July 2022}}</ref><ref name=Nifty>{{cite web|title=Nifty Fifty|url=http://www.usasciencefestival.org/theniftyfiftybios|access-date=12 October 2011|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120429035609/http://www.usasciencefestival.org/theniftyfiftybios|archive-date=29 April 2012}}</ref> He earned his BS in [[physics]] from [[Princeton University]] and a [[PhD]] in [[astrophysics]] from the [[California Institute of Technology]].<ref name=SETI>{{cite web|title=Shostak, Seth|url=http://www.seti-inst.edu/about-us/staff/shostak-seth.php|publisher=SETI Institute|access-date=12 October 2011|archive-date=26 January 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110126114240/http://www.seti-inst.edu/about-us/staff/shostak-seth.php|url-status=live}}</ref>

== Professional work==
Shostak used [[radio telescope]]s in the US and the Netherlands, searching for clues to the [[ultimate fate of the universe]] by analyzing galaxy motion. In 1999, he produced twelve 30-minute lectures on audio-tape and video titled "The Search for Intelligent Life in Space" for [[The Teaching Company]]. An updated overview about the search for extraterrestrial life was presented in 2019.<ref name="NBC-20191004">{{cite news |last=Shostak |first=Seth |author-link=Seth Shostak |title=We may be closing in on the discovery of alien life. Are we prepared? - New robotic craft bound for Mars should give us our best shot at finding life on the Red Planet. |url=https://www.nbcnews.com/mach/science/we-may-be-closing-discovery-alien-life-are-we-prepared-ncna1062176 |date=4 October 2019 |work=[[NBC News]] |access-date=5 October 2019 |archive-date=5 October 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191005140438/https://www.nbcnews.com/mach/science/we-may-be-closing-discovery-alien-life-are-we-prepared-ncna1062176 |url-status=live }}</ref>

=== SETI Institute===
Since 2001, he has been the senior astronomer at the SETI Institute, a not-for-profit organization whose mission is to "explore, understand and explain the origin, nature and prevalence of life in the universe". SETI Institute, located in [[Mountain View, California]], employs over 50 researchers that study all aspects of the search for life, its origins, the environment in which life develops, and its ultimate fate.

He was the chair of the International Academy of Astronautics SETI Permanent Committee from 2003-2012.<ref>{{cite web|title=IAA SETI Permanent Committee: Minutes|url=http://avsport.org/IAA/minutes.htm|website=avsport.org|access-date=2016-10-26|archive-date=2018-07-22|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180722055149/http://avsport.org/IAA/minutes.htm|url-status=dead}}</ref>

== Public outreach==
[[File:CSICON 2011-Seth Shostak (cropped).JPG|thumb|Shostak in 2011]]
Shostak is an active participant in the Institute's observation programs and, along with Molly Bentley, co-hosts the weekly radio show ''[[Big Picture Science]]'', which was produced by the SETI Institute from 2002 until January 2025 when it went independent.<ref>{{cite web|last=Seth|first=Shostak|title=Big Picture Science|url=http://bigpicturescience.org/|publisher=SETI Institute|access-date=25 January 2014|archive-date=30 January 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140130101108/http://radio.seti.org/|url-status=live}}</ref>   Each week, Shostak interviews guests about the latest scientific research on a variety of topics: [[physical cosmology|cosmology]], [[physics]], [[genetics]], [[paleontology]], [[evolutionary biology]] and [[astrobiology]]. ''Big Picture Science'' is distributed on the [[Public Radio Satellite System]] and the [[Public Radio Exchange]] and is available for download at the show's website and through podcasts.

Shostak also co-hosts the "Skeptic Check" episodes of Big Picture Science, focused on debunking [[pseudoscience]], [[Unidentified flying object|UFOs]] and practices such as [[astrology]] and [[dowsing]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Big Picture Science|url=http://radio.seti.org/pages/about_the_show|work=About...Big Picture Science|access-date=12 October 2011|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111001041153/http://radio.seti.org/pages/about_the_show|archive-date=1 October 2011}}</ref>

He has published four books, nearly 300 popular articles on astronomy, technology, film and television and gives frequent talks to both young and adult audiences.<ref>{{cite web|last=Shostak|first=Seth|title=Seth Shostak: ET is (probably) out there -- get ready|url=https://www.ted.com/speakers/seth_shostak|publisher=Ted.com|access-date=2014-01-27|archive-date=2014-01-23|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140123025254/http://www.ted.com/speakers/seth_shostak.html|url-status=live}}</ref>

==Recognition==
Shostak was the 2004 winner of the [[Klumpke-Roberts Award]] of the [[Astronomical Society of the Pacific]] in recognition of his outstanding contributions to the public understanding and appreciation of astronomy.<ref name=GALE>{{cite news|title=Seth Shostak|newspaper=Contemporary Authors Online|location=Detroit|publisher=GALE Literature Resource Center|date=2010}}</ref>

In January 2010 he was elected as a fellow of the [[Committee for Skeptical Inquiry]] (CSI),<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.csicop.org/news/show/sixteen_notable_figures_in_science_and_skepticism_elected_csi_fellows/ |title=Sixteen Notable Figures in Science and Skepticism Elected CSI Fellows |date=12 January 2010 |access-date=2011-08-07 |archive-date=2011-08-05 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110805022638/http://www.csicop.org/news/show/sixteen_notable_figures_in_science_and_skepticism_elected_csi_fellows |url-status=live }}</ref> and in October 2019 was a featured speaker at the organization's annual conference, [[CSICon]].<ref>{{cite web |title=CSICon 2019: Speakers |url=https://csiconference.org/speakers/ |website=CSIconference.org/ |publisher=CFI |access-date=25 October 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191025181214/https://csiconference.org/speakers/ |archive-date=25 October 2019}}</ref>

He has been an observer for [[Project Phoenix (SETI)]] as well as an active participant in various international forums for SETI research. He served as chair of the [[International Academy of Astronautics]] SETI Permanent Study Group from 2002 to 2012.<ref>{{cite web|title=IAA SETI Permanent Committee|url=http://www.setileague.org/iaaseti/|publisher=The SETI League|access-date=13 October 2011|archive-date=27 September 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110927061232/http://www.setileague.org/iaaseti/|url-status=live}}</ref>

Shostak has been nominated by the [[SETI Institute]] to be one of the [[USA Science and Engineering Festival]]'s Nifty Fifty Speakers, who will speak about his work and career to middle and high school students in October 2010.<ref name=Nifty />

==Personal life==
Seth became interested in [[electronics]] and [[amateur radio]] as a young student.<ref name=TEDx>{{cite web|title=ET is (Probably) Out There — Get Ready|date=2 June 2012 |publisher=TED|url=https://www.ted.com/talks/seth_shostak_et_is_probably_out_there_get_ready?}}</ref>

Shostak's hobbies include film making, railroading, and computer animation. While working at the [[University of Groningen]] in the [[Netherlands]], he founded [[:nl:Digima|DIGIMA]], a computer animation company.<ref name=GALE /> He is a brother of [[Robert Shostak]], developer of the [[Paradox (database)|Paradox relational database]].{{Citation needed|date=October 2020}}

In the spring of 1988 Seth left [[Groningen]] to help his brother, who was then working on image database software in [[Silicon Valley]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://docs.google.com/document/d/1jFnlfuQ5_ikH3CqYz6Ahvt89w9S-3fiZVcWjC_eQoUA/pub |language=nl |title=Nieuwsblad van het Noorden |date=March 25, 1988 |access-date=2013-03-22}}</ref>

According to his C.V., Shostak has a considerable body of creative writing, mostly for corporate clients. He was also "idea man" behind a plan to build a large space and technology theme park in The Netherlands and also the Air and Space Exhibit at the [[California Science Center]], where he also serves on the board.<ref>{{cite web|last=Shostak|first=Seth|title=Curriculum Vitae|url=http://www.seti.org/sites/default/files/Shostak-CV2009.pdf|access-date=2014-01-27|archive-date=2013-06-03|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130603220738/http://www.seti.org/sites/default/files/Shostak-CV2009.pdf|url-status=live}}</ref>
